note: Adapted from the original English description in Banks 1919. The original describes it as Anoplotermes schwarzi, sp. nov., and records only the alate (Winged), giving no measurements and no soldier or worker description; the type is in the U.S.N.M. (MCZ Bulletin 62, OCR of the whole volume), from Cayamas, Cuba, 19 May (month 5) (Schwarz leg.). The original gives only the comparison with A. fumosus and the wing venation, recording neither absolute measurements of the head and pronotum nor body colour; nothing has been added in this entry.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Similar to A. fumosus Hagen, but the head and especially the pronotum are wider, and the ocelli are slightly farther from the compound eyes. The pronotum is about as wide as the head between the eyes, anterior margin nearly straight, sides curving smoothly into the rounded posterior margin. The media of the wing has a rather long apical fork; the cubitus has 10 branches; behind the radial sector, toward the wing apex, there are faint traces of cross-veins extending nearly to the middle of the media. The original description is based on the alate only; soldiers and workers are not recorded.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The original (Banks 1919) gives the diagnostic characters in a single 'Winged.' paragraph and lists no measurements; the holotype is recorded as U.S.N.M., from Cayamas, Cuba, 19 May (Schwarz leg.).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The type was collected at Cayamas, Cuba, by Schwarz on 19 May (month 5); the holotype is in the U.S.N.M. The original records on the same page the distribution of Leucotermes tenuis (Hagen) in the Bahamas, Cuba, Haiti, Puerto Rico and Jamaica, which is irrelevant to this entry.
